providers.name: Google Play (GMS)
providers.desc: For devices with Google Play services. Uses Google Maps and Google location services.

providers.name: Huawei AppGallery (HMS)
providers.desc: For Huawei devices without Google Play services. Uses Huawei Map Kit, Location Kit and ML Kit (document scanning) instead.

variants.name: SDK without tracking
variants.desc: Only the Almatar SDK. No analytics, attribution, engagement or session-replay tools are included, and the SDK's analytics calls do nothing.

variants.name: SDK with tracking tools
variants.desc: The Almatar SDK plus the optional com.almatar:analytics-tracking add-on. Tracking runs only inside the Almatar flows (hotel, flight and bookings screens). The add-on registers itself at app startup, so no code changes are needed.

flows.name: B2C
flows.desc: Consumer integration. Initialize with enableB2bSDK = false and launch any of the hotel / flight / bookings flows directly.
flows.init:
AlmatarAppInitializer.init(
    application = this,
    baseUrl = "<your base url>",
    almatarEnvironment = AlmatarEnvironment.Production,
    supportNumber = "<support number>",
    almatarUiConfig = AlmatarUiConfig(),
    enableB2bSDK = false,
)

flows.name: B2B
flows.desc: Corporate (e.g. Aamal) integration. Initialize with enableB2bSDK = true and a brandName. Same launch flows as B2C, with the corporate section enabled on payment.
flows.init:
AlmatarAppInitializer.init(
    application = this,
    baseUrl = "<your base url>",
    almatarEnvironment = AlmatarEnvironment.Production,
    supportNumber = "<support number>",
    almatarUiConfig = AlmatarUiConfig(),
    enableB2bSDK = true,
    brandName = "<your brand>",
)

flows.name: B2B with SSO
flows.desc: Corporate SSO integration. Initialize in B2B mode, then hand the SDK a short-lived SSO token via launchB2BSsoBookings. Only the SSO bookings entry point is valid in this flow.

payment.intro: Every launch function that opens a search or booking flow (`launchFlights`, `launchFlightsSearchResults`, `launchHotels`, `launchHotelsSearchResults`) takes `startPaymentFlowImpl`. It decides who takes the payment when the user taps pay. The SDK checks the price, and any coupon, first.

modes.name: Pay through Almatar
modes.summary: Pass `startPaymentFlowImpl = null`. Almatar shows its own payment screen, charges the user and confirms the booking. Your app has nothing else to do.
points: The payment screen lists the payment methods Almatar has enabled for your account, such as card, Tabby or Tamara.
Coupons, wallet and loyalty points are hidden in SDK mode.
After a successful payment the SDK shows its booking confirmation screen.
modes.code:
AlmatarAppInitializer.launchHotels(
    locale = LOCALE.ENGLISH,
    almatarFlowFinishedCallback = { /* the user left the SDK */ },
    generateTokenImpl = { callback -> callback(token, refreshToken, null) },
    startPaymentFlowImpl = null, // Almatar takes the payment
)

modes.name: Pay through your app
modes.summary: Pass a `startPaymentFlowImpl` function. The SDK hides its payment methods, and when the user taps pay it calls your function with the booking. You charge the user in your own checkout, then report the result back through `paymentFlowCallback`.
points: `bookingId`: Almatar's booking ID. Keep it with your payment record.
`amount`: the total to charge, in the booking's base currency.
`bookingKey`: the key that identifies the booking in Almatar.
How the money you collect reaches Almatar (settlement and invoicing) is agreed with the Almatar team. It isn't set in the SDK.

states.name: LOADING
states.desc: The SDK shows a loader over the payment screen.

states.name: SUCCESS
states.desc: Report it only once the charge is confirmed. The SDK shows its booking confirmation screen.

states.name: CANCELLED
states.desc: The user stays on the payment screen and can pay again.

states.name: FAILURE(message)
states.desc: The SDK shows your message on the payment screen. The user can pay again.

postBooking.summary: Add-ons bought after booking from My Trips (for example seats or baggage) are always paid through your app. Pass `startPostPaymentFlow` to `launchBookings`. Without it, the add-on checkout closes. On `SUCCESS` the SDK shows the add-on confirmation; on `FAILURE` it shows your message and closes the checkout.

payment.otherFlowsNote: Payment in this flow always goes through Almatar: `launchB2BSsoBookings` has no payment parameter.

customization.intro: SDK screens follow the `almatarUiConfig` you pass to `AlmatarAppInitializer.init`. Every field is optional: leave one out to keep Almatar's look.

sections.title: Brand colors
sections.summary: Pass your brand colors in code with `colors = AlmatarColors(...)`, instead of overriding Almatar's color resources in XML. Each color fills every Almatar color that plays that role, so you set a few colors, not each resource.

fields.name: primary
fields.desc: Buttons, links, selected tabs and icons.

fields.name: primaryContainer
fields.desc: A light tint of `primary` behind chips, inputs and selected cards.

fields.name: overrides
fields.desc: Any other Almatar color: a map from `com.almatar.core.R.color.*` to a color. Applied last.

codes.label: Fixed colors
Material 3 theme

points: Each SDK screen reads the colors when it opens. Call `setColors` again when your theme changes, for example for dark mode. `setColors(null)` goes back to Almatar's colors.
Covers Compose screens, colors set in code, and colors in XML layouts and styles, including state selectors in `res/color`.
Icons and shapes drawn from XML drawables keep Almatar's colors for now.
Overriding `almatar_*` colors in your own `colors.xml` still works. Where both apply, colors passed in code win.

sections.title: Logo
sections.summary: Set `logoRes` to a drawable from your app, PNG or vector, to show your logo where the SDK shows Almatar's.
points: Shown in the gift box on the payment screen (40dp) and in the header of the corporate registration screen.
Use an image that still reads at small sizes. A square mark works best.

sections.title: Background, bars and back button
sections.summary: Match the screen background, status bar, toolbar and back button to your app.

fields.name: backButtonRes
fields.desc: Drawable for the toolbar's back button.

codes.label: Kotlin
codes.code:
almatarUiConfig = AlmatarUiConfig(
    backgroundConfig = AlmatarBackgroundConfig.DrawableResource(R.drawable.app_background),
    statusBarConfig = AlmatarStatusBarConfig(colorConfig = AlmatarColorConfig.Transparent),
    toolbarConfig = AlmatarToolbarConfig(configColor = AlmatarColorConfig.Transparent),
    backButtonRes = R.drawable.ic_back,
)

versions.notes: First tracking-free release: the tracking tools moved out of core-gms into the optional com.almatar:analytics-tracking add-on. Pin this exact version. Gradle ranks 1.0.0-alpha01 below 1.0.5, so a version range or 'latest' resolves to 1.0.5, which still bundles the tracking tools.
